subject.title: acp: assistant text corrupted when Gateway revises in-progress output (non-append revision mis-sliced)

question: How should the ACP bridge represent Gateway `replace: true` revisions when standard ACP message chunks cannot retract already-emitted text?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the durable behavior depends on whether maintainers prefer buffering, a client-specific replace extension, or a fallback that may show corrected text separately.

options.title: Choose conservative buffering
options.body: Buffer or delay unretractable provisional ACP output where Gateway replacement revisions are possible, then emit a final append-only sequence that matches the authoritative text.

options.title: Use a replace extension
options.body: Adopt an ACP metadata or capability extension for clients that understand replacement semantics and document fallback behavior for clients that ignore it.

options.title: Accept fallback duplication
options.body: Emit corrected replacement snapshots as new ACP output even if some clients may show both stale and corrected text.

recommendation.title: Choose conservative buffering
recommendation.body: Buffer or delay unretractable provisional ACP output where Gateway replacement revisions are possible, then emit a final append-only sequence that matches the authoritative text.

likelyOwner.reason: ACP support traces to this owner and the choice crosses the ACP/Gateway protocol boundary rather than being a purely mechanical slice fix.
